now how do I send this html-based email using gmail?

Gmail's compose window can't take raw HTML, so you have two options.

**Option 1: Copy and paste (quickest, fine for a few recipients)**
1. Replace the placeholder logo `src` with a publicly hosted PNG URL, because Gmail won't load local files.
2. Open `~/Desktop/canvas-mcp-invite.html` in Chrome.
3. Press ⌘A, then ⌘C.
4. In a new Gmail message, press ⌘V, then add the subject and recipients.
5. Send a test to yourself first.

What you lose this way: the `<style>` block, so no dark-mode overrides, and possibly the preheader. Gmail keeps most inline styles, but it can change the button's rounded corners and padding a little.

**Option 2: Google Apps Script (sends the exact HTML, works for a list)**
1. Upload the HTML file to Google Drive.
2. Go to script.google.com, create a new project, and paste:

```js
function sendInvite() {
  const html = DriveApp.getFilesByName("canvas-mcp-invite.html").next().getBlob().getDataAsString();
  const recipients = ["[REDACTED_EMAIL]"]; // or read from a Sheet
  recipients.forEach((to) =>
    GmailApp.sendEmail(to, "Help test the official Canvas MCP server", "Sign up: https://forms.gle/jXYJN6NNQFnaYCPa8", {
      htmlBody: html,
      name: "Instructure Product Team",
    }),
  );
}
```

3. Run `sendInvite`, and allow the Drive and Gmail permissions when asked.
4. Test with just your own address first.

The third argument to `sendEmail` is the plain-text version, shown by clients that can't display HTML.

**Tips:**
- For a large list, loop through the recipients as the script does, or use a mail-merge add-on like YAMM or GMass. Don't put everyone in To or CC.
- Gmail has daily sending limits: about 500 recipients a day for personal accounts and 2,000 for Workspace. For bigger sends, use an email service instead.
- Test in the Gmail web app, the Gmail mobile app, and Outlook before the real send.
what about with 'Mail' on my mac?

Apple Mail can't paste in raw HTML either, but Safari can hand it the rendered page.

**Recommended: Safari's "Email This Page"**
1. Replace the placeholder logo `src` with a publicly hosted PNG URL.
2. Open the file in Safari: `open -a Safari ~/Desktop/canvas-mcp-invite.html`.
3. Choose **File → Share → Email This Page**, or press ⌘I.
4. Mail opens a new message with the page in it. Make sure the format popup in the header says **Web Page**, not Reader or PDF.
5. Add the subject and recipients, send a test to yourself, then send.

This sends the whole HTML document, so it keeps the `<style>` block for dark mode. Whether dark mode actually works still depends on the recipient's email app.

**Also works: copy and paste**
Open the file in Safari, press ⌘A and ⌘C, then paste into a new Mail message. It's quick, but it can drop the dark-mode styles and the hidden preheader.

**Things to know:**
- **Don't edit the body in Mail after it loads.** Typing in it can scramble the table layout. Only change the subject and recipients.
- **Mail may attach the logo instead of linking it.** It sometimes embeds remote images as attachments, which is fine, but check the test email.
- **AppleScript isn't an option.** Mail's scripting doesn't reliably support HTML bodies.
- **Mass sending:** Mail has no mail merge, so send one message with everyone in BCC. For a large list, the Gmail script or an email service is better.

content.text:
I added a second logo for dark mode, and the email switches between the two automatically.

- **Light logo:** `https://example.com/canvas-horizontal-color.png`. It shows by default, including in any email app that can't switch for dark mode.
- **Dark logo:** `https://example.com/canvas-horizontal-reversed.png`. It stays hidden until the reader's device is in dark mode, then replaces the light one. Outlook desktop never shows it.

For the dark version, use pantoken's `reversed` variant (`plugins/pantoken/logos/assets/logos/canvas/horizontal-reversed.svg`), which is made for dark backgrounds. Export both logos as PNG at 310×78 so they stay sharp on high-resolution screens, host them, and replace the two placeholder URLs.

Gmail won't switch logos. It either keeps the light logo or recolors the whole email on its own, so give the light logo a transparent background so it still looks acceptable in Gmail's dark mode.
can I use an svg?

Only for readers using Apple's email apps. Most other email apps won't show an SVG. | Email app | SVG in `` | | --- | --- | | Apple Mail (macOS, iOS) | Yes | | Outlook for Mac and iOS | Mostly | | Gmail (web, apps) | No, shows alt text or a broken image | | Outlook for Windows, Outlook.com | No | | Yahoo, AOL | No | Embedding the SVG code directly in the HTML, or as a `data:` URL, is supported even less widely, and Gmail strips both. Since you can't control which email app your readers use, stick with PNG. You don't even need to host your own copies of the SVGs to start from. They're already public on jsDelivr, which you can open and export to PNG: - `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/plugin-logos/assets/logos/canvas/horizontal-color.svg` - `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/plugin-logos/assets/logos/canvas/horizontal-reversed.svg` To make the PNGs, open each SVG in Preview or a browser and export it at 310×78 with a transparent background, or run `rsvg-convert -w 310 horizontal-color.svg -o canvas-horizontal-color.png` if you have librsvg installed. Then host the PNGs and replace the two placeholder URLs. If you know nearly everyone reads on Apple devices, you could put those jsDelivr SVG URLs straight into the two `src` attributes. Gmail and Outlook readers would then see only the "Canvas" alt text.

No, that link won't work for your recipients. I requested it while signed out, the way a recipient's email app would, and Google returned `403` (access denied) with an HTML page instead of an image.

The `/u/0/` in the URL means it only loads for a signed-in Google account, so everyone else would see a broken image. Google Sites image links can also stop working over time.

Better places to host it, where the link loads for anyone and doesn't change:

- **Your email service or company CDN.** This is the best option if you have one.
- **A public GitHub repo.** Use the raw file URL, such as `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/main/canvas-logo.png`, or `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/<org>/<repo>/canvas-logo.png`.
- **An image host** like Imgur or Cloudinary. Use the direct link that ends in `.png`.

Google Drive isn't a good choice either. Its share links go through a redirect and viewing limits, and some email apps won't load images that way.

Once it's hosted, check the link by opening it in a private browser window. If the image shows up without signing in, send me the URL and I'll put it in the `src`.

now give me the steps to send it as an email using apple mail.

1. **Open the email in Safari**, not Chrome, because Safari is the browser that can hand a page to Mail:
   ```sh
   open -a Safari ~/Desktop/canvas-mcp-invite.html
   ```
2. **Choose File → Share → Email This Page**, or press ⌘I. Mail opens a new message with the page in it.
3. **Check the format.** At the right end of Mail's subject line, there's a small popup. Make sure it says **Web Page**, not Reader, PDF, or Link Only.
4. **Fill in the header fields:**
   - **Subject:** something like "Help test the official Canvas MCP server".
   - **From:** your sending account.
   - **To:** your own address for now.
5. **Don't click into the body.** Editing the email in Mail can scramble the layout.
6. **Send the test to yourself and check it** in Apple Mail, and on your phone or in Gmail if you can:
   - The logo loads.
   - The "Sign up" button is centered and opens the form.
   - The "Follow along" link works.
7. **Send the real email.** Press ⌘I in Safari again for a fresh message. Put your own address in **To** and the recipients in **Bcc** so they can't see each other's addresses. If Bcc isn't showing, choose View → Bcc Address Field.

If Safari's File → Share menu has no "Email This Page," add Mail under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Extensions → Sharing.

If Mail flags the message as large, choose **Actual Size** in the image-size popup at the bottom right of the message window.
